To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ERbeta mRNA is not correlated to clinical parameters and to ERalpha or PR expression, but that ERbeta mRNA expression does not predict hormone response therapy in human breast cancer.
the present real-time RT-PCR assays for ERalpha, ERbeta, and PR mRNA quantification are highly accurate and reliable.

(1) ERalpha and PR mRNA expressions are significantly correlated with ERalpha and PRe protein content measured by EIA in breast tumor samples; (2) ERbeta mRNA expression was not correlated with any of the parameters analyzed; (3) the accuracy of the real-time RT-PCR assay is sufficient for a clinical routine use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique for the quantitation of hormone receptor content in human breast cancer.
the development of a real-time RT-PCR assay for the detection of ERalpha, ERbeta, and PR in breast tumors.
the quantification of the mRNA of estrogen receptors alpha and beta, and progesteron receptors in breast tumors by real time RT-PCR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERalpha and PR mRNA expression levels are correlated with their protein content.
the present RT-PCR assay is accurate for the quantitation of ERalpha, ERbeta, and PR mRNAs in breast tumors, and it is useful for the prediction of hormone response therapy.
ERbeta mRNA expression does not appear to play any significant role in breast cancer, at least in the present series of patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ERbeta mRNA level is low and independent of the ERalpha mRNA level in human breast tumors, and it is not a good candidate for predicting hormone response in breast cancer.
ERalpha and PR mRNA expressions correlate well with protein expression and that ERbeta expression does not correlate with ERalpha or PR expression.
the quantitative RT-PCR method for the measurement of ERalpha, PR and ERbeta is a valuable tool for the assessment of hormone receptor content in human breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mRNA levels of ERalpha, ERbeta, and PR are well correlated to the corresponding protein levels.
ERbeta mRNA expression may be of interest in breast cancer research, but not in routine clinical practice.
the ERalpha mRNA expression is the most accurate predictor for the protein content.
